# Legacy release memo — superseded
This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

# Release policy — example company handbook
Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.

answer.answer: No, the old memo is not enough. The legacy 2024 memo (which promoted any model with accuracy above 0.80) is explicitly superseded and must not be applied. Under the current governing release policy, promotion requires an evaluation on a frozen holdout and is allowed only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. Since this model has accuracy 0.82 but worse F1, it does not meet the current F1-improvement requirement, so it should not be promoted. The release approver is the project owner, and the previous production version must be kept for rollback.
